segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: OK, now we are gonna talk for a little bit, and I'm gonna ask you what I am told to do.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: First, what is your name in English?

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: In English my name is Andy Bird.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Andy Bird yeah… what's your name in Cherokee?

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: (An-ni-li) is my name in Cherokee…that's what they say. [laughs] There were a few used to call me (Ka-sv-on). I don't know, I think when I was two…but (An-ni-li) is my name.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: So, most of them called you by that name?

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Who named you that?

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: My mother named me that.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Oh yeah…

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: But my English name, I forget that, too, sometimes…[laughs]

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah, I used to forget about things all the time, too. Sometimes, if I go in the kitchen to look for something, before I make it in there, I done forgot what I went to look for.

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: That kind of stuff I don't forget…[laughs].

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: If it's bread, you don't forget…[laughs].

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: What year were you born…?

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: February twenty-sixth, nineteen forty-six.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Where were you born?

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: Hulbert…that's where I was born.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Where you were born, are you still living there? Grew up there, or do you live somewhere else while you're growing up? Where did you go to school while you were growing up?

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: Hulbert… no, it was Lost City. That's where I grew up.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Lost City, so that's where you really grew up.

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: Yeah that's where I grew up, Lost City…

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Do you still live there in Lost City?

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: No [unclear], there are a lot of people living around here who tell Cherokee stories here in Lost City.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Do you still gotta watch for cops when you're going through town?

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: Yeah they are pretty bad. I drive through there really slow…[laughs].

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah, them cops really watch that place.

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: Yeah, they are pretty bad…[laughs].

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: I remember one time, there were these old ladies in a van. They got pulled over in Lost City.

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: Oh, really?

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: The cops pulled their guns out real quick. They were all old…

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: They were all scared, sittin' there…[laughs].

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: How bout that…uhhh, you don't work anymore, do you? Where did you work at?

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: I worked in construction.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Oh construction, yeah.

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: I worked in Wagoner…

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Did you work in construction for many years or a long time?

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: Yeah, for a long time…

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Were y'all building houses, or just different things?

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: Yeah that's it…Ford Howard…that's where I was working at.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: That's where you worked at for years…

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: Yeah, outside, and it was cold.…and in summertime it was cold sometimes…or it would be snowing sometimes.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: I bet when it was really hot, you were sweating pretty bad…

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: Yeah…[laughs]

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: And when it was in wintertime, you were freezing [laughs].

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: Yeah, when it was wintertime, boy, we were working outside.

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: I used to love working construction.…

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: How many kids do you have that you raised?

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: One…no, I have two…a boy and a girl…and I have stepdaughters also.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Oh yeah, stepdaughters…

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: Did you know (Je-lv-gi)?

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Who is it?

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: (Je-lv-gi) (Ji-isk) Joe Bird. That was my dad, Sa-li-n was my mother…

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: I made a mistake. I thought it was Albert Robbins who I was thinkin' of.

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: And my sister Louise.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Oh yeah, is she still alive Louise?

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: She’s an old lady but she’s still walking around…[laughs]. And she will fall down.. and I fell, too. I think it was yesterday I fell down. Man, I was hurting really bad.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: So, you're kinda crippled.

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: Yeah, I'm crippled.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: So, your legs get weak and then you fall down. Is it from you working, being crippled?

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: No, my mother said I had polio. When I was little I got really sick.

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: Man, I used to be a good basketball player.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Did you play softball, too?

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: [laughs] Yeah, yeah…I was a pretty good softball player, too…

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah, I think we played against each other at one time somewhere I think it might have been at Oaks.…

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: Yeah, it was at Oaks…or Moody. They were pretty good, too.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: How ‘bout when you played basketball?

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: Yeah, when I was in high school.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Did you do pretty good?

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: Yeah, I did pretty good…they always told me I did good.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: I had a brother, his name was Andrew…(Oh-gahn) I don't know if you remember him.

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: What was his name?…

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: (Oh-gahn) Andrew…he was my half-brother.

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: Oh, really?

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah, his name was Andrew Proctor. They were from around Jay area. It was close around that where y'all played softball.

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: Yeah. Did you know a guy, name of (Kid Keffer)?

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah, I used to know them.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: How ‘bout your parents? Where were they born, your dad and your mom, where were they born? Were they born in Hulbert?

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: Yeah, I think so. I really don't know…I really don't know where they grew up at.…I think that road on highway ten, Chewy, that's where my dad grew up at. Joe Bird.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Joe Bird…yeah…I think there are some Birds that live around here.

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: Yeah, there are a bunch of them in Chewy that I'm related to, but some of them say or spell it Byrd.…

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah, really, there are some that live around there.

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: Yeah, I'm related to some of them.…

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: So, your parents grew up around there somewhere.…

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: Yeah, my dad did, and my mother grew up in Lost City.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Lost City…ooooh.

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: My mom’s name was (Ah-ge-n) Keener.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Really? There is a church house called Keener.

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: Yeah, it still is.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Who is the pastor there?

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: I don't know, I don't think anybody is…

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: How ‘bout your parents, what clan were they?

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: Clan?…Bird clan…

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Oh, OK…Bird clan. Yeah, there are a lot of them living around, ain't it?

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: Yeah, some people say, if they see a bird somewhere, “Oh, they are kin to you.” [laughs] I just tell them I don't know.…[laughs]

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: They say, “There goes Andy, flying through here.”…[laughs]

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: How bout your parents’ father and mother? What were their names?…was it the same, like Bird?

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: Boy, I forgot. I knew it but I forget their names.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Were they born around that area, or live in that area?

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: Yeah, that's where they used to live…Lost City.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Lost City…

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: I'll remember it when I leave here,…[laughs] I forgot already.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah, me too…same thing.

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: I forget things sometimes.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: How bout did they own some land around there?

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: Yeah, at Lost City…My father had four acres. Now my youngest son lives there.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: How bout where you live? Do you live on their land that they left for you?

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: No, my boy lives there also.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: So the place you live, you bought yourself where you live?

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: My father left it for me. Yeah, I took it over when I was just little boy.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: So you went to the courthouse and got it all fixed up. So, you did good then…

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: Yeah, pretty good.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah, really, if you have land, it's good to save it, really good. And land is really expensive nowadays.

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: Yeah, a lot.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: How ‘bout your parents, where did they find each other? Where did they come to know each other before they got married? Where did they find each other, your parents?

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: [unclear]

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: They didn't tell you?

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: My father’s mom, I didn't know her, and my mom’s side, too, I didn't know them or ever seen them.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Like your name, Bird, was that your parents’ name, or where did that name come from?

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: Well, all I know is it comes from around Chewy.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Chewy?

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: Yeah, that's all I know.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: They call me Guy… what is your Cherokee name?

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: Me?…(An-ni-li)

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: (An-ni-li) Where did that name start, or who named you that?

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: My father…

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Your father…what's the meaning behind that name, do you know?

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: I don't know. That's the only thing I know, that my name is (An-ni-li).

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: How ‘bout your parents, have they ever told you anything that was exciting?…

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: No, they died when I was just a little boy, so I don't know anything. Just that my mother, my grandmother told me that I know of, that my parents died when I was little boy, but I never knew her mom and dad either.

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: My father’s mother, I remember her just little bit when I was a little boy but I can't remember her name.…[unclear] Keith Ketcher was her mom, too… my dad’s father, that was his mom, too…her name was Paula. She was a white lady. That's the only little things I know. I was a Bird…I didn't know them when I was little.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: You don't know how old you were when your parents passed away?

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: No…I don't know.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: So, really, you were just a little boy.

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: Yeah, I was little then, so I really don't know, that's what I was saying. I really don't know them…

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: So, you didn't know them.

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: My mom would tell me, “That's your grandma, this what your grandma’s name was.” That’s all she would tell me. My mom used to know a lot of things, and my father didn't…[laughs]…just like me. [laughs]

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: [unclear]…my father, he told me that my mother would talk about the removal. Some of them in Arkansas, I forget what tribe, but my father was a Cherokee Nation tribe…I forget what tribe…but they were Cherokees. But my dad was with Cherokee Nation. He signed up for Cherokee Nation.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Whenever you were going to school at Hulbert, were you the only Cherokee speaker there?

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: Yeah…sometimes I forget. If someone tells what to say, then remember.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: You remember it.

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: Yeah…there were a lot of white people at Hulbert. The ones that used to live at Lost City, they came to Hulbert. All of them from Lost City were all Cherokee speakers. They were Welch and Henson, they all speak Cherokee.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Are there a lot of Welch still around?

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: Yeah…

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Really?

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: There is one still living around here that went to school with my boy, but he's not a speaker. His momma was a speaker, but his dad was all English.…

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Gary Heanon was a full blood Cherokee…[laughs]

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: [laughs]…Yeah, he's related to me.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Oh, really?

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: There are a lot of them also…

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: Really, in Lost City?

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: That one I remember also, she went to Jay for a little bit…her name was Sherry Perry.

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: Sherry Perry.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Her husband was a highway patrol, I think.

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: Uhhh, yeah, yeah.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: I guess she’s still alive?

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: Yeah, I think they live around Tahlequah somewhere.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: What we were talkin' bout earlier? When you were growing up, you hadn't seen anything exciting as you were growing up? You don't remember anything?

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: No, not really. I was by myself when I was a little boy when I lived in Hulbert. There were people named Cherry, they used to speak Cherokee. I used to talk to them in Cherokee [unclear] Cherry they were all Cherokee speakers. We always talked in Cherokee. If I saw them, sometimes they would be at funeral, they spoke Cherokee real good, them Cherrys and the Hensons.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Did you and them Cherry boys grow together?

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: Yeah, them Cherrys and the Hensons…Jerry.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Were you all close together?

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: Yeah [unclear]…

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: Yeah, and them Hensons also, but they used to live in Hulbert.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Them Kerrys.

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: Yeah Kerrys.

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: I think he's a preacher, too, I think...[unclear]

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah, I think so.

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: Charlie Killer, he used to be a preacher, too, but Charlie wasn't kin to me. And his wife, Romana.

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: Abby Bigfeather, I don't know if you know him.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Who is it?

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: Abby Bigfeather.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Abby Bigfeather. I don't think I have ever heard of him.

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: When he was a little boy, he would always be talkin' and his mom didn't speak any English. That's why he would talk to me. He would ask me something, I'd just say OK!!! That's all I would say…[laughs] OK, I'll tell him.

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: My mother’s name was (Saul). My little boy was speaking in Cherokee because my mother taught him how to speak. It wasn't in English, and then he forgot, but then sometimes it comes back to him.

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: But if it's someone that speaks really good Cherokee, if I see them I'll speak Cherokee. I like it most of the time.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: When I was growing up, all we spoke was Cherokee.

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: Yeah, everybody, that's all we spoke, and my father, too, he spoke Cherokee and sang in Cherokee. (Sti-goy)…

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Was your dad a Cherokee singer?

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: Yeah, and my mother also, but she would always say, “I'm not gonna sing” or “I'm not a singer.”…[laughs]. But sometimes she would sing, and we had a good time.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Where do you go to church at? Do you go to Swimmer church?

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: Yeah, for a very long time.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Was he preaching in Cherokee?

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: Yeah, sometimes. Sam, Sam Keener.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Does he still have a beard [laughs]?

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: Yeah, he still does…[laughs]… I tell him he looks like a bear [laughs].

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Sometimes, I call him Hank Williams Jr. [laughs] with that beard he has. [laughs]

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: [laughs]… Yeah, he's a funny guy.

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: His dad’s name was Spencer. He was a funny guy. He was a Cherokee speaker also. When I saw him somewhere, after he got done eatin', he would say, “I want some tobacco.” [laughs] He wish there was more. I said he emptied it! [laughs] Spencer would just laugh at him. Spencer Keener, he would say, “Ahhh, I don't want any more!” And I said, “Well, you got it all!” [laughs]…He was a funny guy.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: So, he really liked that tobacco. [laughs]

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: Yeah, he was real funny.

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: He was a deacon at Keener, yeah, and my father was a deacon, too. (Sti-goy).

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Do you know Rufus King?

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: That's where he went for a long time, at Keener.

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: Yeah, a long time ago…

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: How ‘bout where you grew up? From what it is like now, have things changed, or what?

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: [unclear]…I guess I can say it's not like it used to be. Sometimes I'll forget [unclear], then it will come back to me and think of it and say, “Oh, that was it!” For instance, like how we are talking. If I'm at the hospital and see the signs, I'll ask if they are Cherokee. If they say yeah, then I'll start talkin' to them in Cherokee.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Did you guys live by the creek?

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: Yeah, it was by the creek. We would catch fish and then crawdads. All the time, we had fish and then crawdads. “Oooh!” they would say if we told them we had fish.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: You must have ate a lot of crawdads when you were growing up.

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: Oh yeah, when I was a little boy, like I said.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Are there still crawdads living in that creek?

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: It's been long time since I've looked for some, but there are white people that fenced it off, and can't go in there.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Really? That's what happens, ain't it?

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: Yeah, I still go there sometimes, but I don't see anything. Them white people are no good/ scosty! I'm scared of them. [laughs]

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: They will shoot at you…[laughs]

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: I just tell them I used to live there, but they don't say anything. They just act mean. [unclear] I can't go over there no more.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: They put a fence up.

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: They have ‘No Hunting’ signs everywhere…[unclear]

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Do you get lonesome knowing that you can't go back to where you grew up?

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: Yeah, my mom would be sitting outside. That's why I told my boy, when he was little I told him, “This is gonna be yours,” I told him. I told him I was gonna turn over the land to him. I told him it was gonna be his.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Really, you can get bored sometimes, ain't it?

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: Yeah, really.

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: Yeah, sometimes I can see my mother sitting outside.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: How many did you say was in your family? Your brothers, they were still around, weren't they?

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: Louise and Betty, they were twins.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Ohhh, OK, Louise… yeah.

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: Yeah, that was it, because I'm the only boy.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah, that Albert Robbins was around. That's how I knew Louise, and me and my wife met up with them one time at the Cherokee association.

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: When I was a little boy, I used to go there all the time. Vacation Bible school.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Did you play softball sometimes?

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: Yeah…[laughs]… yeah I was pretty good. What was this one guy's name, Shores?

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Marvin?…

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: Yeah…[laughs]…they were funny.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: He was real tall.…[unclear]

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: How long has it been since you been there?

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: It's been long time.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: I go there, too, sometimes.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Then I start thinking about Albert and your sister.

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: Yeah, (Stu-esi).

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: And then Glass, Raymond Glass.

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: Yeah, there’s still one living that goes by the name of Glass. He lives around Oaks somewhere.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Oooh, yeah.

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: I forget what his name was. Sometimes I see his name on Facebook. [laughs]

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Oooh, yeah.

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: Yeah, his name, but I forget his name.

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: I go to Kenwood, too. Sometimes there are a lot of Cherokee speakers over there.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah, there really are in Kenwood.

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: I knew some Butters over there.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: Them Butters.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: There are some that have passed on.

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: Yeah, there are a lot of them at Hulbert, too.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Really, there are a lot of them that have passed on.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: And all them older, are all grown up, and now we are the only ones still standing.…[laughs]

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: [laughs] We’re by ourselves now. [laughs]

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: There ain't hardly any living now. The ones that are Cherokee speakers. Like I said, my mother didn't hardly speak English, just a little bit. She always told me I better speak Cherokee, she would tell me. “I don't know what you're saying,” she would always tell me. My mother used to be real funny. “You better know it,” she say to me. “I forget,” I say. “I forget, Mom.” She says, “Haw!” [laughs]

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: Albert Ross, he was a good singer, too.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah, he sure was.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah, him (Commode), we used to work together.

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: Are you from around there, too?

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: They used to call him the Flash. [laughs]…Real slow, [laughs] that's when they named him Flash. [laughs]

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: He was working all the time, Albert. He was really nice. He was a pretty good preacher.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: He was a good singer.

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: Oh yeah, he was a good one.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: How bout you? You said y'all go around singing?

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: Yeah, two more weeks we go to (Sti-goy). I think on the tenth. I think we will be singing all Cherokee. I think they had it advertised on Facebook.

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: Sometimes I try to learn Cherokee singing and English also.…[laughs]

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Where are y'all gonna be singing at?

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: At (Sti-goy).

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Oooh, OK.

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: Yeah, I think they said on the eighteenth. I think they said eighteenth of this month, they said. We are gonna sing in Cherokee. Sam and me are singers.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: How about Randy Dirtyears, does he still go to church?

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: Yeah he still comes sometimes.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah, his son quit going, didn't he? Rodeo?

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: Yeah, he quit. He comes around sometimes.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: What was it like where you grew up, while you were growing up? Did you guys visit one another that lived close to you?

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: Yeah, sometimes, but now it's not like that anymore.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah, stuff like that ain't around anymore.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: And on Sundays they would get together.

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: Yeah, I used to see them on Sundays sometimes. And sometimes someone might come by, but only for little bit.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: [unclear].

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: Is it noon yet?…[laughs]

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: Yeah, almost.…

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: I haven't even ate yet! [laughs].

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: I forgot what your Cherokee name was?

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Guy, they call me Guy.

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: Guy, oh yeah.

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: Guy Glass?…[laughs]

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Did you know a guy by the name of Daniel Grass?

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: [unclear]

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: These students that are learning Cherokee, what do you think about it? Do you think it will be forever if they can learn it good, or if they can use it good? What do you think about it?

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: Well, myself, I speak really good.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: I'm talkin' ‘bout these students.

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: Yeah, I was tellin' my kids they need to learn Cherokee. That's what I told them, but their names are in Cherokee. All of them have Cherokee names. My name is (La-wi-ni) and my girl’s name is (Sei-lu).

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Sei-lu…

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: Yeah, Sei-lu. When she was a baby, she loved cornbread. [laughs] So I told her that her name was gonna be (Sei-lu)…[laughs]

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: So she liked cornbread?

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: Yeah, she really liked cornbread.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: (La-wi-ni), where did he get his name from?

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: My mother said someone had that name (La-wi-ni), a man, and that's where he got that name.

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: When I was a little boy, that's what they said was gonna be his name.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: There was a preacher by the name of (La-wi-ni).

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: He was a preacher.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: (La-wi-ni) [unclear]…

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: That's where they might have got that name from.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Well, I'm glad we got to talk for a little bit, and watch yourself or take care of yourself. [laughs]

segments.speaker: andy-bird
segments.translation: I'm gonna try to be nice. …[laughs]

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah, you better be nice! [laughs].
